 Number of flood victims in Selangor rises, Perak records slight drop

 KUALA LUMPUR: The number of flood evacuees sheltering at temporary relief centres in Selangor continued to rise on Saturday morning (Nov 21), while Perak recorded a slight decrease, with only one relief centre still operating in Negri Sembilan.
 In SELANGOR , the number of flood victims increased to 1,869 from 522 families placed at 13 relief centres this morning, compared with 1,764 evacuees from 482 families on Friday night (Nov 20).
 According to the Social Welfare Department's InfoBencana portal, the relief centre at Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Dato' Maharaja Lela is sheltering the highest number of victims at 401, followed by SK Parit Mahang (365); Sekolah Rendah Agama (SRA) Bukit Kuching (224); Bukit Kuching Tengah Community Hall (143); SK Rantau Panjang (134); SRA Batu 8 Ijok (120);
 SK Sultan Abdul Aziz (187); SK Jaya Setia (97), Kafa Integrasi Hidayah Bukit Cherakah (66), Seri Harmoni Community Hall (62), SK Sungai Binjai (25); SK Batu Arang (25); and Balai Raya Kampung Sungai Kelambu (20).
 In PERAK , the number of evacuees housed at eight relief centres in five districts dropped slightly to 499 people from 169 families, compared with 500 from 172 families on Friday night (Nov 20).
 The State Disaster Management Committee (SDMC) secretariat said Kerian district recorded the highest number of evacuees, with 164 people from 52 families housed at the SK Bukit Merah and SK Parit Haji Aman relief centres.
 In Manjung, 131 victims from 39 families are still sheltering at the Sekolah Rendah Agama Rakyat Padang Serai relief centre, while in Hilir Perak, 97 evacuees from 31 families are placed at the Teluk Intan Municipal Council's Dewan Rumah Rehat relief centre.
 Meanwhile, in Perak Tengah, 92 victims are taking shelter at the SK Dato' Sagor dan SK Tanjung Belanja relief centre, while in the district of Larut, Matang and Selma, 15 evacuees from six families are housed at the SK Batu Hampar relief centre.
 The Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has forecast fair weather throughout Perak on Saturday morning, although thunderstorms and rain are expected in the afternoon and evening.
 In NEGERI SEMBILAN , only one relief centre is still operating in Port Dickson, with SK Jimah housing 39 victims from 12 families as of 8.46am on Saturday.
 Based on the InfoBencana portal, the victims comprise 16 men, eight women and 15 children, including infants. – Bernama
